title: The Nonengagement Strategy: Trade Space for Time
coreMove: Yield ground you can afford to lose so time, endurance, and overextension begin working against the stronger side.
sourcePressure: When the opponent is stronger, standing on their chosen ground wastes force; withdrawal buys time only if there is strategic depth.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Retreat from a position that has no survivable ground to trade.

sourceAnchors.name: Russian campaigns against Napoleon and the Wehrmacht
sourceAnchors.detail: the source says Greene draws nonengagement from Russian campaigns that traded territory for time against Napoleon and later the Wehrmacht.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The Russian lesson is not romance about retreat; space only helps when the retreat buys time the other side cannot afford.

hook: Do not open with a battlefield metaphor for The Nonengagement Strategy: Trade Space for Time.
Do not start by saying strategy is not about violence.
counterintuition: Avoid the reusable correction frame that the move is not X but Y.
Avoid a bland paradox about strength looking like weakness.
tryThisNow: No generic timer, pause, breathe, or list-three-options prompt.
No reusable ask what matters most prompt.
examples: No generic founder in a pitch deck unless the domain requires it.
No battlefield reenactment or invented historical anecdote.
